blocks.text: At the alley, Billy stopped with one hand on the railing.
Nobody waited at the top of the steps. He looked along the roofs for Fist, then down into the sunken yard. The basement service door was shut.
Seth knew where they were supposed to meet. Billy had been delayed, but the boy should still have been here.
He took out his notebook and checked the address once more. Right building. Right entrance.
That did not make the empty steps any better.
blocks.alt: Billy, in his plaid deerstalker and high-collared tan trench coat, looks down the alley steps into the empty sunken service yard, where the basement door is closed.

blocks.text: Billy went down slowly. At the bottom, he stood beside the door rather than in front of it. He listened.
A scrape reached him through the metal, followed by a voice too muffled to make out. He waited for another. Somewhere farther inside, something clicked.
He kept his hand away from the handle.
Warm light moved across the upper bricks. Billy looked up.
Flaming Head hovered above the yard, his face plain inside the curling fire. His eyes moved from Billy to the closed door.

He had gone to Jenny’s roof and found the drum beside the wall, with nobody practicing. Billy’s office window had been empty too. Remembering their warning about Daniel, he had come to look around the laboratory building. From above the alley, he had seen Billy on the steps.
Billy pointed toward the service door. “Jenny came for an interview. She didn’t call back. Seth was supposed to wait for me up there.”
He looked toward the roofs again. “And I can’t find Fist.”
Flaming Head’s expression changed. Warmth reached Billy, but no words he could understand came with it. He shook his head.
“I can’t hear you the way they can.”
Flaming Head looked toward the narrow basement window. Billy followed his gaze, then raised a hand toward the door and held it still.
“Stay out here.”
Flaming Head nodded. He had promised Jenny he would not go into the laboratory alone. He stayed in the yard.

Billy watched him drift along the wall to the high window. For a moment, Flaming Head looked in from the upper corner. Beyond the bench, he could see the two chairs and the steel around their occupants. Daniel was bent over his notes. Luke faced his uncle.
Flaming Head moved clear of the opening and settled beside the outer brick jamb. The projecting stone edge screened his fire from the room. Billy could still see his face from the yard.
Inside, Seth felt a familiar warmth.
He lifted his eyes only as far as the bench. Jenny had gone still beside him.

On the roof, they had always been looking at Flaming Head when he spoke to them. Here they could see only the yard’s brick wall through the small high window. With him so close on the other side, the warmth carried his words all the same.
“Keep looking where you are. I’m outside.”
Seth nearly said his name.
He closed his mouth.
Jenny turned her eyes toward Seth. The smallest lift of her eyebrows was enough. She had understood too.

Only Seth and Jenny could make sense of the message. Fist lay low in his locked cage, his torn white cuff folded beneath him. Luke’s iron teeth clicked as he waited for Daniel’s pencil to stop. Neither turned toward the window.
The collector’s loose wire still lay across the bench. Its glass was empty.
blocks.alt: Seth and civilian Jenny exchange a subtle hopeful glance while all their wrist and ankle cuffs remain closed. Injured Fist lies in one locked cage beside the empty, unfinished collector; the high window shows the yard’s brick wall.

blocks.text: “Remember the drum,” Flaming Head told them. “Slow down. Choose one thing. Stay with it.”
Seth looked at his right wrist.
The cuff had not changed since Daniel last checked it. His hand was still inside, his red glove pressed against the armrest. He set his thumb beneath one edge without pulling his shoulders forward.
His head still ached. When he tried to hurry, the room seemed to move.
He stopped pushing and let it settle.
Across the bench, Daniel rubbed out another line.
“What are you rubbing out now?” Luke asked.
“Something that doesn’t belong there.”
“You put it there.”
Daniel brushed the eraser crumbs toward the edge. “Do you want me to leave it wrong?”
Luke looked past him at the collector. “I want to know when you’re going to help me.”
Seth waited until their attention was back on the paper. Then he pressed again, slowly, keeping his eyes on the place where steel met glove.
The chair stayed quiet.
Jenny let one shoe tip within the little movement the ankle cuff allowed. Then the other. Her legs felt heavy, and she could not find the rhythm she had managed on the roof.
She rested, watching Luke instead of her feet.
When she tried again, she kept the movements small. A faint point flickered in the shadow beneath her chair. She let her feet settle, and it vanished before she could gather it into a ball.
Her shoes stayed inside the closed ankle cuffs. She did not try to kick.

Fist shifted his scuffed leather against the cage floor. Jenny glanced toward him. One eye opened, then narrowed at Luke. He had received no reminder from the window, and the effort of moving still hurt him.
Three firm knocks sounded at the service door.
Daniel’s pencil stopped.
“Dr. Orkleson.” Billy’s voice carried through the front room. “I want to speak to Jenny.”
Seth’s thumb slipped.
He left it where it was and waited for his breathing to slow.
Luke rose toward the workshop doorway. Daniel held up a hand.
“Stay with them.”
“It’s Billy.”
“I know who it is.” Daniel put the pencil down. “He’ll want an explanation. I can give him one.”
“Then give me one first.”
Daniel looked from Luke to the boy’s chair. “We’ll talk when I’ve dealt with this.”
“You keep saying that.”
Another knock came.
“Jenny,” Billy called. “Can you hear me?”
Jenny drew breath. “I’m here, Billy.”
“Then come to the door.”
“He’s fastened me to a chair.”
Daniel turned sharply toward her.
Billy’s next words were quieter, but firm. “Open the door, Daniel.”
Daniel straightened his coat. He walked through the workshop doorway, past the rolled-aside shelf and into the front room.
Luke stayed beside the stations. He looked at Jenny, then at Seth. “You heard him. Stay where you are.”
Fist pushed his battered knuckles against a cage bar. “Been working on that.”
Luke’s eyes moved toward the cage.
Outside, Billy stepped back from the service threshold before the latch moved.

He had seen Flaming Head settle beside the window. He did not know what the captives had heard or what they might be trying. He wanted Daniel away from them, and he wanted to know what had happened to Jenny.
The door opened a few inches.
“Billy.” Daniel’s glasses caught the light from the yard. “There’s been a misunderstanding.”
“I heard Jenny.”
“She became upset during the demonstration.”
“She said you’ve fastened her to a chair.”
Daniel opened the door a little farther. “Come in. We can discuss it.”
Billy stayed on the flat yard landing, clear of the doorway. “Bring her out.”
Daniel kept one hand on the door.
Beside the window, Flaming Head remained behind the projecting brick and stone. His face was visible from the yard, but Billy kept his eyes on Daniel.
Inside, Seth put his attention back on the cuff.
He remembered holding the drum steady while Jenny watched. He had wanted to look at her then, too. This time, he kept his eyes on the steel.
He pressed with his thumb and the side of his gloved hand. Slowly. The chair did not rattle.
Luke turned away from the cage.
Seth felt the edge give.
Only a little. The steel was beginning to bend, but the cuff stayed closed around his wrist. His hand was still secured to the armrest.
blocks.alt: Seth applies controlled pressure with his red-gloved hand to a slightly bowed but still closed steel wrist cuff. His hand remains secured as Luke’s floating blond head and iron jaws turn toward him.

blocks.text: His fingers stayed over the bent edge as Luke turned toward him.
